newsitem.title: GERMANY: German beet test positive but weather very dry.
newsitem.headline: German beet test positive but weather very dry.

text.p: The second German beet test of the 1997/98 campaign shows the crop has made good progress over the last two weeks but this could be overriden by overly dry weather, a source at industry association WVZ said.
"Leaves are looking healthy and a crop of medium to good quality may be harvested," he said.
"But that assumes the dry conditions won't last forever."
Pan-German rainfall over the last two weeks was only 13 mm on average compared with 29 mm in the comparable period last year, WVZ data showed.
In the states of Rhineland-Palatinate and Thuringia, no rain was received versus 17 mm and 27 mm respectively last year.
Otherwise, the test showed a better theoretical sugar yield of 6.24 tonnes per hectare (tph) (6.07 last year) while sugar content of 15 percent was identical with the number last year.
The first test a fortnight ago had shown a lower yield and a lower sugar content compared with the first test in 1996.
Monday's sugar yield result was above long-term averages (1983-1996) in the second test of 5.95 tph in western Germany and 5.33 tph in eastern Germany (1991-1996).
Monday's sugar content of 15.0 percent compared with a western German 1983-1996 average of 14.9 percent and an eastern German 1991-1996 average 15.5 percent in the second test.
The beet area this year totals 508,687 hectares after 514,452 ha in 1996/97.
